lines.t: [Intro - city rain, Rhodes, distant trumpet]
Two in the morning.
Windows burning all across the skyline.
So many lights...
And so many people afraid of the dark.
Last train carries somebody's daughter home,
Man on the platform talking to a silent phone.
Top-floor window, somebody can't sleep;
Down on the pavement, somebody can't eat.
We built another tower, put a garden on the roof,
Still don't know what to do with an inconvenient truth.
Every screen is selling something hunger cannot hold.
We can light a thousand windows.
We can't make a heart less cold.
I came up here to pray about the state the world is in,
Then remembered every window has a life behind the skin.
Not a headline. Not a number.
Not a point I need to prove.
Someone waking up tomorrow
Who has never tasted being loved.
My heart breaks when My children forget Me.
Says The LORD.
[Silence - one low piano chord]
And suddenly the city
Wasn't distant anymore.
I couldn't pray for thunder
Without hearing something more.
Under all these satellites,
Under all this restless blue,
There are hearts that keep on reaching
For a home they never knew.
YahuShua-YAHUWAH,
Let the night awaken me—
Not to love the coming ruin,
But to long for what will be.
When the weapons fall silent,
When the frightened finally sleep,
When the earth is full of knowing
Who has loved us all this deep.
[House Lift - rolling bass, trumpet answering vocal]
A watchman isn't posted just to stare into the black,
Counting every fracture, never looking at the map.
There's a promise past the shaking,
There's a purpose past the fall.
If I only preach the breaking,
Have I listened to it all?
Not a kingdom built on corpses
For another man to own.
Not the powerful replacing
Other powerful men on thrones.
I am waiting for the ending
Of the need to make men bleed.
For a child to cross a meadow
With no reason to be scared.
And I cannot build that Kingdom
With the force of my own hand.
But I can stop rehearsing
All the cruelties of man.
I can put away the insult.
I can answer without spite.
I can tell the truth in daylight
That I sing about at night.
Behold, I shall cleanse the sanctuary
and restore the garden,
and you shall learn war no more—
NO MORE!
Says The LORD.
[Drop - radiant house groove, immense male harmonies]
No more sons to the slaughter!
No more names beneath the stone!
No more mothers at the doorway
Waiting for a step toward home!
Let the trumpet carry warning!
Let it carry longing too!
I don't only want the darkness gone—
I want the world made new!
Made new...
Not another coat of gold.
Made new...
What no empire ever owned.
Made new...
Not another coat of gold.
Made new...
What no empire ever owned.
[Break - beat dissolves, close voice]
Sometimes I get so tired
I forget what hope sounds like.
I mistake my disappointment
For the measure of Your might.
And sometimes I want the ending
Just to end what hurts in me.
But Your love is not my anger
Given heavenly authority.
Let me wait without becoming
What I'm praying You will end.
Let me mourn without forgetting
How to welcome, how to mend.
Beloved of My heart,
be not troubled nor weep,
for these things must be.
Then the end shall come,
and I shall reveal My glory.
Says The LORD.
[Build - heartbeat, strings, orbital arpeggios]
Then put breath back in the warning.
Put thanksgiving in the wait.
Put a song inside the service
When the morning finds me late.
Let me walk into the city
With Your Word and open hands.
Not announcing my importance—
Just obeying what I can.
There is somebody to listen to.
There is someone I can feed.
There is mercy I can practice
While the whole creation grieves.
Under all these satellites,
Under all this restless blue,
I will lift my eyes in worship
And my hands in service too.
Let me walk into the city
With Your Word and open hands.
Not announcing my importance—
Just obeying what I can.
There is somebody to listen to.
There is someone I can feed.
There is mercy I can practice
While the whole creation grieves.
Under all these satellites,
Under all this restless blue,
I will lift my eyes in worship
And my hands in service too.
YahuShua-YAHUWAH,
All the glory is Your own!
Not the towers we have fashioned,
Not the greatness of our names!
You shall bring the promised morning.
You shall make the violence cease.
I will not confuse my hurry
With the coming of Your peace.
A garden where nothing is destroyed,
And none are given to destruction;
No more pain or tears,
no more sickness or death...
Only life is,
and shall be,
forever!
Says The LORD.
The city hasn't changed yet.
The first train shakes the ground.
I fold the page.
I leave the rooftop.
There's somebody downstairs
I can love right now.
